metadata.name: Peter Bird PB2002 computed plate motion vectors
metadata.citation: Bird, P. (2003). An updated digital model of plate boundaries. Geochemistry Geophysics Geosystems, 4(3), 1027. doi:10.1029/2001GC000252.
metadata.poleSource: scripts/pb2002-euler-poles.json (transcribed from Table 1, page 6 of the published PDF)
metadata.referenceFrame: Pacific-plate reference frame (PB2002 Table 1); the Pacific plate itself has zero velocity by definition
metadata.velocityModel: v = omega x r on a sphere of radius 6371.0088 km; km/Myr is numerically equal to mm/yr
notes: Each feature is a sample point inside a PB2002 plate polygon with the linear velocity computed from that plate Euler pole.
Major plates carry multiple sample points so their velocity gradients are visible; small plates carry fewer.
All poles and boundary geometry come from the same PB2002 model, so plates and motions are internally consistent.
Euler vectors are stated with high precision to avoid round-off, but their true accuracy is lower (Table 1, footnote a).

poleMetadata.name: Peter Bird PB2002 Table 1 - plate identifiers, areas, and Euler poles
poleMetadata.citation: Bird, P. (2003). An updated digital model of plate boundaries. Geochemistry Geophysics Geosystems, 4(3), 1027. doi:10.1029/2001GC000252
poleMetadata.sourceLocation: Table 1, page 6 of the published PDF
poleMetadata.transcription: Values transcribed programmatically from the published PDF text layer (pdftotext -raw). The PDF minus sign is an unmapped glyph; it was read as U+FFFD and interpreted as negative.
poleMetadata.referenceFrame: All poles are expressed in the Pacific-plate reference frame. Rotation about each pole is counterclockwise when seen from outside the Earth.

columns.name: Plate name
columns.omegaDegPerMyr: Rotation rate, degrees per million years (counterclockwise positive)
columns.reference: Source publication of the pole estimate

validation: Pacific (PA) pole is 0/0/0, the identity of the Pacific reference frame.
Nazca (NZ) pole 55.578/-90.096/1.3599 and North America (NA) pole 48.709/-78.167/0.7486 match the published NUVEL-1A values (DeMets et al. 1994) verbatim.
All 52 rows parse with latitudes within +-90, longitudes within +-180, and rates within [0, 60] deg/Myr; no duplicate codes.
poleMetadata.note: Euler vectors are stated with high precision to avoid round-off error in differencing, but accuracy is much less (footnote a of Table 1).
